subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service raw-stream disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override persisted state-dir `.env`, config env, or generated LaunchAgent service-env entries, or should those persisted sources remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain prompts and tool output, so automation should not choose the operator-control boundary or migration behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat `0`, `off`, `false`, and unset/removed launchd disable intent as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config env as the durable source until the operator edits those files or config, and document that launchctl unset alone is not enough.

options.title: Doctor-Only Repair
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged, but add doctor/status checks that warn about and repair raw-stream service-env drift before operators rely on disable state.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat `0`, `off`, `false`, and unset/removed launchd disable intent as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The raw-stream helper and central runtime path came through his recent merged OpenClaw runtime work, and the decision crosses runtime, service env, docs, and security boundaries.
